title: kv-cache: improve memory manager and eviction policies for spillover/paging/fragmentation
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: We continue to see cases where KV cache fragmentation and unbounded spillover degrade tail latency and increase GPU memory pressure under heavy concurrent prefix workloads. This PR refactors the KV memory manager to track fine-grained fragments, introduce an adaptive compaction heuristic, and add a paging-aware eviction policy that prefers cheap-to-reload pages for spillover. The goal is to reduce long-tail eviction churn, lower OOM events, and improve steady-state throughput. Changes include: 1) refactor runtime/kv_cache/memory_manager to maintain per-allocation fragment metadata and a fast free-list for coalescing; 2) introduce EvictionTier and PageCost estimators to differentiate small high-reuse fragments from large low-reuse pages; 3) implement adaptive compaction that triggers when fragmentation exceeds a threshold or when expected spillover cost crosses a dynamic threshold; 4) add a paging mode that serializes low-cost pages to host memory in background I/O threads; 5) expose two knobs (kv.cache.compaction_threshold and kv.cache.paging_budget) for ops tuning and diagnostics; 6) add unit and integration tests, and a microbenchmark for fragmentation workloads. Backwards compatibility: default knobs preserve current behaviour. Rollout plan: staged rollout on dedicated clusters with canary enabled and telemetry dashboards to monitor fragmentation_ratio, spillover_rate, compaction_latency, and eviction_cost. See linked Linear tasks for tuning plan.

Feat: add EvictionTier and PageCost estimators

review_comments: Ava Chen: Can we avoid a global lock in the hot eviction path? The perf numbers look good but locking cost may regress under high concurrency.
Sofia Martinez (author): Reworked eviction hot path to use per-core free-lists and optimistic try-lock; added microbench showing <2% overhead on 64 concurrency cores.
Liam O'Connor: Suggest making compaction_threshold a percentage, not absolute bytes, to be robust across instance sizes.
Sofia Martinez (author): Converted compaction_threshold to a ratio (0-1) and added automatic scaling for GPU memory sizes in the config parsing; updated docs.
Maya Patel: Unit tests look good; one integration test flakes locally due to timing of background pager.
Sofia Martinez (author): Increased pager backoff and added deterministic test hook to disable background thread in unit runs. That removed the flake.
Ava Chen: Approved after verifying perf runs and safety checks on a canary cluster.
merge_summary: Squash merged by Ava Chen. Commit message: kv-cache: improve memory manager and eviction policies for spillover/paging/fragmentation - refactor fragments, add adaptive compaction, background pager, and expose tuning knobs.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: reduced fragmentation, adaptive compaction, and paging for spillover to host memory. Operators can tune kv.cache.compaction_threshold and kv.cache.paging_budget. Expected impact: fewer OOMs under heavy prefix workloads and reduced eviction churn.
notes: Performance: microbenchmarks show 15-25% reduction in eviction churn and 8-12% lower average token latency in fragmentation-heavy workloads on our internal GPU clusters. Ops: Recommend enabling canary for 48 hours and monitoring fragmentation_ratio and spillover_rate before wide rollout.
